faq.metaDescription: Common questions parents ask about Bingoo — ages, safety, devices, pricing.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: What parents often ask about Bingoo.

0.a: Bingoo is an online learning platform for kids aged 6–15 that turns lessons into games, with a personalized path and Bingoo as a friendly buddy.

1.a: Content follows the curriculum for kids aged 6 to 15 and adapts its difficulty to each child's level.

2.a: Yes. Content is moderated, there are no ads, and parents get screen-time controls.

3.q: What devices can my child learn on?
3.a: Bingoo runs in the web browser, on tablets and phones — just sign in and pick up where you left off.

4.a: There's a Free plan to get started; Plus and Family unlock the full experience. See the Pricing page for details.

5.a: You can cancel anytime from your account settings — no fees, no strings attached.

q1.hint: Give both fractions a denominator of 4.

q2.explain: An even number is divisible by 2.

q3.prompt: The Sun rises in the East.
q3.explain: The Sun always rises in the East.

q6.prompt: Match the expression to its result

q8.guide: Tap the words in order. Tap again to remove.

q9.explain: Fish and shrimp live in water; chickens and cats live on land.

q10.prompt: Tap the nouns in the sentence

q11.prompt: Mark the number 13 on the number line

q12.prompt: Set the clock to half past 3
q12.explain: The short hand is between 3 and 4; the long hand points to 6.

q13.prompt: Sort the animals into the right circle
q13.explain: Birds/bees can fly; dogs have 4 legs; a fish fits neither.

q14.explain: Cork and leaf float; the coin sinks.

q15.prompt: Show the number 7 on the ten-frame

q17.prompt: Build the number 43 with tens and ones

q18.explain: The pattern repeats: red, blue, red, blue…

q19.prompt: Drag each name onto the right fruit

q20.explain: The cat 🐱, dog 🐶 and bird 🐦 are animals.

q21.prompt: Draw an arrow from each animal to where it lives

q22.prompt: Find the hidden words: tap the first then the last letter
q22.explain: CAT 🐱, DOG 🐶, PIG 🐷 and SUN ☀️ are hidden in the grid.

q23.prompt: Shade 3/4 of the circle (tap the parts)
q23.explain: 3 out of 4 parts are shaded — that is 3/4.

q24.prompt: Sort each animal into the right cell (legs and flying)
q24.explain: Cat/dog: 4 legs, cannot fly. Bird/bee: not 4 legs, can fly.

q26.prompt: Pick US coins to make exactly $2.50

q27.prompt: Pick UK coins to make exactly £1.20

q28.prompt: Which side has more apples? Pick the right sign.

q29.prompt: Build the chart: how many like each colour (red 3, blue 5, green 2)

q30.prompt: How long is the pencil? Tap the tick at its end.
q30.explain: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at tick 6 → it is 6 cm long.

q31.prompt: Draw the other half to make it symmetric (tap the cells)
q31.explain: Every cell on the left has a mirror cell across the axis on the right.

q32.prompt: Use the pen to circle or draw your answer (open response)
q32.explain: This is an open response — your teacher reviews what you drew.

q33.prompt: Count the vehicles, record with tally marks (groups of 5)

q34.prompt: Each 🚗 = 2 cars. Fill the pictogram (red 8, blue 12)
q34.explain: Red 8 cars = 4 icons; blue 12 cars = 6 icons.

q35.prompt: Build an array to show 2 × 8 = 16 (tap the dots)

q36.prompt: The arrow points up. Turn it a quarter turn clockwise — where does it point?
q36.explain: A quarter turn clockwise: up → right.

q37.prompt: What temperature does the thermometer show? (tap a tick)
q37.explain: The colour stops at the 40 mark → 40 °C.

q39.prompt: Get the turtle 🐢 home 🏠 (tap a neighbour to move, tap back to undo)
q39.explain: Go around the blocked cells to reach the target.

q40.prompt: Fill the crossword from the clues

q41.prompt: Work out 1/2 + 1/4 (type a fraction or a decimal)

q42.prompt: Read this sentence aloud, then record
q42.text: The cat sat on the mat.
q42.explain: Open response — record your voice; the teacher reviews it (ASR grading can come later).

q43.prompt: Place each event on the likelihood scale
q43.explain: A walking carrot: impossible. Rain somewhere: might. Sunrise: certain.

q44.prompt: Shade squares to make a shape with area 6 and perimeter 10 (one piece)

q45.prompt: Shade exactly 4 squares to make a pattern symmetric about the vertical line
q45.explain: Every shaded square needs its mirror — e.g. (0,0)&(0,3), (1,1)&(1,2).

q46.prompt: Tap ALL the faces of the cube
q46.explain: A cube has 6 faces — 3 are hidden, so you must turn it.

q47.prompt: Tap ALL the edges of the pyramid
q47.explain: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges: 4 base + 4 slanted.

q48.prompt: Use the identification key to name this animal
q48.subject: What animal is this?
q48.k3: Does the animal have smooth, wet skin?
q48.explain: A frog: no fur → no feathers → smooth wet skin → **amphibian**.

q49.prompt: Find and correct the 2 mistakes (tap a wrong word, then type the fix)
q49.explain: "like play" → **like playing**; "enjoy to swim" → **enjoy swimming**. (Editing a correct word costs a mark.)

q50.explain: The first number is the HORIZONTAL distance (x), the second is VERTICAL (y). (3,5) ≠ (5,3)!

q51.prompt: Write the coordinates of the 4 marked points

q52.prompt: Drag the arm to make a 60° angle
q52.explain: 60° is an acute angle (less than 90°). Tolerance ±5°.

q53.explain: 120° is more than 90° and less than 180° → **obtuse**.

q54.prompt: Draw the line graph: playground temperature (8, 12, 14, 15, 11 °C)
q54.explain: Tap the right height at each time; the points join into a line. 15 °C sits BETWEEN gridlines — that is fine.

q55.prompt: Draw the dot plot: children by age (3, 8, 13, 12, 12, 3)
q55.explain: A dot plot is the same as a line graph but the points are NOT joined.

q56.prompt: Shade the waffle: 40% red, 35% blue, 25% green
q56.explain: A 10×10 grid = 100 squares, one square = 1%. Pick a colour then shade that many.

speech.micDenied: Could not access the microphone. Please allow mic permission.

quiz.solidHint: Drag to turn the solid — some parts are hidden behind!

q57.prompt: Translate the shape 4 squares right and 2 squares down (use the arrows)
q57.explain: Press → four times and ↓ twice. Every square of the shape moves the same distance — no turning, no resizing.

q58.prompt: How far has the shape moved? (describe the translation)
q58.explain: Compare any square of the old shape with the matching square of the new one: 3 right and 3 up.

q59.prompt: What direction do you travel from the School to the Park?
q59.explain: The Park is to the right (east) AND above (north) the School → north-east (NE).

q60.prompt: Which net folds up into a cube?
q60.explain: The 2×3 block and the strip of 6 do NOT fold up (the faces overlap). Only the 1–4–1 cross closes into a cube.

q61.prompt: Which solid does this net make?
q61.explain: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles → a triangular prism. Turn each solid to check its faces.

quiz.filterTitle: Pick an interaction type to preview

q62.prompt: Estimate how long the pencil is, THEN measure it
q62.explain: Only the MEASURED value is marked. An estimate is never right or wrong — it just shows how good your sense of length is.

q63.c3: I used a capital letter and a full stop
q63.exemplar: I know 3/6 = 1/2 because if I divide the top and the bottom by 3, I get 1/2. Three out of six parts is the same as one half.
q63.explain: Open answers cannot be machine-marked: you check your own work against the criteria. Meeting 2 of 3 is a pass.

q64.prompt: Draw a plant with all the parts you have learnt
q64.c2: It has a stem and leaves
q64.c3: It has a flower or fruit
q64.explain: No machine can mark a drawing — you tick the criteria yourself. A teacher (or a model) can re-tick them later with no change to the schema.

q65.explain: A "look and choose" question — each choice is a real picture from the media library (R2), no text. The gold star is the first tile.

q66.body: Listen to the teacher, then choose the right answer.
q66.caption: The teacher explaining
q66.explain: A "listen and answer" question — the teacher’s real audio sits in the question body. She opens with "today we learn even numbers".
q66.imgCaption: A pair of socks = 2 → an even number

q67.prompt: Which one is a PAIR (two matching)?
q67.explain: Three choices, three shapes: text + picture, text + picture, and text + a play button. A choice can be text, picture, audio, or any mix. "A pair" (two matching socks) is correct.

lessons.p: A fraction represents part of a whole — for example 1/2 is one half.

lessons.quote: Mathematics is the language of the universe.

blocks.title: Teaching content blocks
blocks.d1: A part of a whole that has been split into equal parts.
blocks.e1: Half a cake is the fraction 1/2.
blocks.d2: The number BELOW the line — how many equal parts the whole was split into.
blocks.d3: Written differently, but worth exactly the same.
blocks.dlg1: I think 1/3 is bigger than 1/2, because 3 is bigger than 2!
blocks.dlg2: No — if you cut a cake into 3 parts, each part is SMALLER than if you cut it into 2.
blocks.psg1: Long ago, in an old forest, there was a tree that would not stand still like all the others.
blocks.psg2: Every night, when the moon rose, it pulled its roots out of the ground and wandered the forest to look at the stars.
blocks.psg3: But the tree did not know that its roots needed the soil to drink. The next morning, its leaves began to wilt.
blocks.gld1: took something out of where it was fixed.
blocks.gld2: go dry and droop for want of water.
blocks.ref2: I can explain how I worked it out.
blocks.ref3: I can find an equivalent fraction.
blocks.disPrompt: Tell your partner about a time you shared food fairly.
blocks.dis1: How many parts did you make?
blocks.dis2: How did you know the parts were equal?
blocks.s1: One half, one half, cut the cake in two,
blocks.s2: Two equal parts, one for me and one for you.
blocks.s3: Four quarters now, put them back as one,
blocks.s4: Fractions are easy, fractions are fun!

mock.s1Para: When a column's sum exceeds 9, we 'carry' 1 to the tens column. This is the core idea of multi-digit addition.
mock.s2Quote: Add the ones first: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 carry 1.
mock.s3ImgCap: Bundles of ten and loose sticks show the 'carry 1'.
mock.s4Callout: Always start from the ones column.

rich.cPara: When a column's sum exceeds 9, we 'carry' 1 to the left column. This is the core idea of multi-digit addition.
rich.cTermDef: The 1 that moves to the tens column when ones reach 10.
rich.cMathCap: Add the ones first, then the tens.
rich.weNote: Always start from the ones column.
rich.quoteText: Maths isn't hard when you break it into small steps.
rich.st1b: Ones under ones, tens under tens.
rich.imgCap: Bundles of ten and loose sticks show the 'carry 1'.
rich.acc1b: Because we keep 1 ten to add in the next column.
rich.acc2b: When each column's sum is below 10.
rich.dlg1t: Why does the ones column become 12?
rich.dlgQ: So where does the carried 1 go?
rich.psg1: Long ago, whenever the ones column filled to 10, a tiny '1' climbed to the tens column.
rich.psg2: Thanks to it, big sums always came out right.
rich.expQ: Will the wooden ball float or sink?
rich.expS1: Drop the wooden ball in water
rich.disPrompt: Discuss: when does addition need carrying?
rich.lyr1: Add the ones, over ten they go
rich.lyr2: Carry a little one, to the next row
rich.lyr3: Add the tens plus one, and we're done
